summary: This diff extends the existing manual-bridge ChatGPT prompt-library workflow with a second generation mode (--mode enduser_domain) targeting (End User Role x Business Domain) combos, plus two new schema columns (End User Role, Industry) and matching ingest validation; it is additive/isolated (docs + two scripts, no schema/migration/auth/payment/security-path touches, no .github/workflows changes), so tier1 is the correct classification. I verified the claims rather than trusting the self-report: all 25 mapped compliance-tracker/src/lib/engines/*.ts filenames actually exist on disk (zero dropped at load time), both --mode capability_gap (regression) and --mode enduser_domain ran successfully end-to-end and produced well-formed request files, and a hand-built test CSV confirmed ingest_chatgpt_promptbatch_response.py correctly accepts a valid row (real <module_slug>_unregistered fallback capability, valid End User Role, registered placeholder) while rejecting an invalid End User Role and a hardcoded company-name literal. The sandbox write path (chatgpt_promptlib_guard.py) is unchanged and still enforces a realpath-resolved, symlink-safe sandbox boundary, and Capability-derived output filenames are constrained to validated values (real capability_registry names or a deterministic module_slug), so there is no path-injection surface introduced by this change. All modified YAML files parse cleanly and both Python scripts compile. Test artifacts I generated during verification (2 extra pending-request .txt files, 1 extra CSV row/file) were removed and the coverage/duplicates reports were regenerated to restore the sandbox to its pre-review state; no repository files were modified (git status clean).
issues: Minor/cosmetic: DEFAULT_INDUSTRIES (scripts/generate_chatgpt_promptbatch_request.py, lines ~106-113) is defined but never referenced anywhere in either script -- dead code, not a functional bug, safe to remove in a follow-up.
